explanation_steps: $$ AB $$ is a diameter, so $$ \angle AQB = 90^\circ $$: $$ QB^2 = AB^2 - AQ^2 = 64 - 16 = 48 $$.
In right $$ \triangle PQB $$: $$ PB^2 = PQ^2 + QB^2 = 144 + 48 = 192 $$, so $$ PB = 8\sqrt{3} $$.
Power of the point P: $$ PR \cdot PB = PA \cdot PQ = 8 \cdot 12 = 96 $$, so $$ PR = \frac{96}{8\sqrt{3}} = 4\sqrt{3} $$ — option B. (Option C, $$ 8\sqrt{3} $$, is PB.)

explanation_steps: A salt that still has a replaceable hydrogen from the acid is called an acid (acidic) salt.
In a bicarbonate such as $$ NaHCO_3 $$, only one H of carbonic acid $$ H_2CO_3 $$ has been replaced by the metal, so one H is left.
So metal bicarbonates are acidic salts by classification (even though a solution of $$ NaHCO_3 $$ is slightly basic). Answer: B.
bank-general-science-matric-2017-q065._why: Bicarbonates (NaHCO3, Ca(HCO3)2) are acid salts: they still contain a replaceable H.

$$ V_{tot} = (10 \text{ cm})^3 = 1000 \text{ cm}^3 = 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3 $$

**Step 2: Submerged Volume ($$ V_{sub} $$)**
One-fourth is above $\rightarrow$ Three-fourths ($$ 3/4 $$) is **submerged**.
$$ V_{sub} = 0.75 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3 $$

**Step 3: Buoyant Force ($$ F_b $$)**
$$ F_b = \rho_{water} \times g \times V_{sub} $$
$$ F_b = 1000 \text{ kg/m}^3 \times 10 \text{ m/s}^2 \times 0.75 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3 $$
$$ F_b = 7.5 N $$
